name: Euro-area economy
summary: Eurostat puts euro-area Q3 GDP growth at 0.4%; final October composite PMI 51.7, down from 53.1 but above 50
state: Eurostat's flash estimate of 30 Oct put euro-area GDP growth at 0.4% in the third quarter and 1.3% on a year earlier (Eurostat). The final HCOB composite PMI for October was 51.7, a four-month low and down from 53.1 in September, but still above 50 (Tasnim, 4 Nov). Both readings sit above the Normal lines; November flash PMIs are due later in the month.
for_you: The euro-area economy is still growing, so job security and business activity across the region are broadly stable. Slowing momentum and high energy prices are the main pressures on households and firms.
rubric_hit: GDP +0.4% q/q positive and composite PMI 51.7 > 50 Normal line

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
Tasnim — Euro zone economic growth slows to four-month low in October

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
